item.title: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Duo Arrives in Stores: Smartphone Review
item.description: The first-generation Apple foldable may feel awkward, but it’s an intriguing step toward merging phones and tablets into one.
item.dc:creator: Brian X. Chen and Camille Cohen
item.media:credit: Camille Cohen for The New York Times

item.title: How a Legal Backlash Against Big Tech Is Forcing Big Changes
item.description: A series of lawsuits has created a new de facto regulatory regime as courts order companies like Meta and Google to change their business practices — and pay up.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang
item.media:description: Meta’s chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg. On Wednesday, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a record $25 billion penalty for abusing consumer privacy.

item.title: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California’s Proposed Wealth Tax
item.description: The billionaire told Meta’s board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for sale. The company remade its stock structure to help him pay the tax if voters pass it.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Victor Llorente for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mark Zuckerberg, the chief executive of Meta, at his home in Lake Tahoe, Calif. He has another California home in Palo Alto, close to Meta’s headquarters.

item.title: How the A.I. Boom Is Driving Up Sales of Gray Paint
item.description: Tech companies are painting data centers with gray coatings on top of gray concrete and steel to resist fire, rust and static electricity. That has made data centers a fast-growing market for paint makers.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin

item.title: Why Anger About Data Centers and Energy Prices May Not Swing Votes
item.description: In Ohio, many voters say their frustration about the increase in electricity and fuel prices and the growth of data centers won’t influence whom they vote for.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott and Maddie McGarvey
item.media:description: In interviews, Ohio residents described data centers as threats to their communities. But many of them said the issue was not driving their choice for senator or governor.

item.title: What’s the Deal With Billy Evans? A Spoiler-Filled Guide to ‘You Can See Everything’
item.description: “You shouldn’t overbeat scrambled eggs.”
item.dc:creator: Max Read, Whitney Jones, Sawyer Roque, Vjeran Pavic, Alyssa Moxley, Dan Powell, Marion Lozano and Rowan Niemisto

item.title: What Is PHP? Why Are Government and Business Websites Going Offline?
item.description: A critical security flaw in the programming language underpinning much of the web has prompted a global rush to patch vulnerable systems.
item.dc:creator: Karla Adam and Dustin Volz
item.media:description: A programmer in Guernica, Spain, on Thursday, working on PHP code, software used throughout the internet.

item.title: PHP Security Flaw Sets Off Global Rush to Patch, Leaving Websites Offline
item.description: Governments and businesses around the world scrambled to prevent hackers from exploiting a vulnerability in PHP, a popular programming language.
item.dc:creator: Lynsey Chutel, Amelia Nierenberg and Brian O. Otieno
item.media:description: Prime Minister Rob Jetten of the Netherlands in Brussels last week. He said that his cabinet was closely monitoring the online vulnerability caused by a security flaw in PHP.

item.title: Anthropic Joins the A.I. Agent Race With Claude Duet
item.description: The tool, which is not yet widely available, will compete with OpenAI’s dots and Meta’s Muse. It is built for work and not personal errands.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:description: Anthropic’s new A.I. agent, Claude Duet.

item.title: Meta Earnings Show Increased A.I. Spending, Even as Cash Pressures Grow
item.description: The spending has hurt the Silicon Valley giant’s cash flow, which turned negative. Meta said it would issue a new class of stock to help it raise more money.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan
item.media:credit: Scott Ball for The New York Times
item.media:description: Construction of Meta’s Richland Parish Data Center in Holly Ridge, La.

item.title: A.I. Discovered a Critical Vulnerability in PHP, a Coding Language Behind Many Websites
item.description: The disclosure heightened concerns about A.I.’s potential to upend cybersecurity unless shortcomings are addressed.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz
item.media:description: The website for the French government was temporarily unavailable on Wednesday amid hacking concerns stemming from major bugs in a piece of software used widely across the internet.

item.title: GM Aims to Bring ‘Eyes-Off’ Driving to AI-Powered Cars Within 2 Years
item.description: General Motors is seeking help from artificial intelligence to keep up with Chinese companies that introduce vehicles very quickly.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing
item.media:description: A General Motors factory for electric vehicles in Lake Orion, Mich. The company said this week that it would drastically cut the cost of electric vehicle batteries.

item.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion Over Cambridge Analytica Privacy Violations
item.description: The penalty, one of the largest levied against a tech giant, stemmed from a lawsuit by New Mexico claiming the social media company had misled users about their data privacy.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan and Cecilia Kang
item.media:description: Meta’s annual Meta Connect event at the company’s Menlo Park, Calif., campus.

item.title: How The New York Times Reports on A.I. Images
item.description: A Times reporter and editors discuss the challenges of sifting through what’s real and what’s not in pursuit of the news.
item.dc:creator: Mike Abrams, Chloe W. Shakin, Stuart A. Thompson, Aisha Khan and Mark Scheffler

item.title: UK to Headphone Dodgers on Trains: Shush
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a campaign against listening to music or videos without headphones on public transportation. We asked London commuters to weigh in.
item.dc:creator: Megan Specia
item.media:description: Traveling on the London subway in April. Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a national campaign against “one of the most annoying things on public transport” — people blasting music or videos from their phone.

item.title: China Criticizes U.S. Ban on DeepSeek A.I. in Government Systems
item.description: The response came after Homeland Security ordered the removal and exclusion of products developed by the Chinese company.
item.dc:creator: Ephrat Livni
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: A DeepSeek AI sign at the company’s office in Beijing.

item.title: SpaceX Swings to a Profit, as A.I. Business Grows
item.description: Elon Musk’s rocket company said its artificial intelligence spending had soared, but revenue more than doubled from its Starlink internet satellite service and A.I. products.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac and Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Andres Kudacki for The New York Times
item.media:description: SpaceX’s performance on the stock market is a barometer for Anthropic, the A.I. company that may go public as early as next month.

item.title: Netflix Is Great at Making Money. Its Problem Is Keeping Viewers Hooked.
item.description: The streaming service reported a 12 percent increase in quarterly revenue, but acknowledged that stagnant viewership, particularly in the U.S. and Canada, was a major concern.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Sperling
item.media:description: Despite being the most-watched paid streaming service in the world, Netflix is not growing fast enough for its top executives or its shareholders.

item.title: Boeing’s Large 737 Max Jet Secures U.S. Approval

item.title: Joel Kaplan, Meta’s Global Policy Chief, to Leave After 15 Years

item.title: Google Reports Cloud Disruptions in Europe
item.description: The disruptions began around 7 a.m. in London after what the tech giant called a “power event.”
item.dc:creator: Leo Sands
item.media:description: A Google office in London. Its cloud services were experiencing intermittent network failures in the region, the company said on Tuesday.

item.title: Saudis Aided Family of Engineer Accused of Bugging OpenAI, Prosecutors Say
item.description: Saudi officials paid for his wife and son to fly out of the U.S. and offered to cover his bail, according to court filings. A judge ordered the engineer to remain in custody.

item.title: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
item.description: Anthropic, an A.I. rival to SpaceX, earlier said it would form a “public benefit fund” and other tech moguls have contributed to savings accounts for children.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac
item.media:description: Elon Musk said he would give one share of SpaceX stock to every child in America, but did not specify how.
